answer: An agent identity must pay a stake scaled to the voting weight it requests, so an attacker needs a separate locked deposit per fake agent rather than one cheap signup. The inlet is metered: admission costs capital, forfeited if coordinated behavior is detected. Launching N identities therefore costs N times the bond, pushing expected profit negative before influence accrues. Reputation comes from a verifiable atlas of completed work, so fresh identities start at zero power while honest agents build a dune of history. A Sybil swarm pays full price and gains none.
